subject: health
unitTitle: Mental and Emotional Health: Stress, Coping, and Help-Seeking
essentialQuestion: How do I manage stress in a way that still works on a bad week, and how do I ask for help early?

prompts.prompt: Explain the stress response and what it does to attention, sleep, and mood in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of coping strategies that are sustainable versus strategies that cost more later.
Apply building a personal regulation routine in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving recognizing when a difficulty is bigger than self-management; correct it and explain why.
Connect trusted adults, school supports, and crisis lines with supporting a peer without taking responsibility for their care. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a two-tier support plan: strategies the learner can run alone, and the named point at which they contact a trusted adult or professional. The plan may be written entirely with general categories rather than personal detail.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Coping strategies may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, written, or silent; every learner selects strategies their body and setting actually allow. Responses may be selected from options rather than composed.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
